caption: I buy airtime R10 at a time and it came to R650. Does anyone else add up the small buys?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R10 400
p/m wages
Living in Ladybrand
slides.body:
Male, 36
Married, two kids (7 and 3)
Job: Petrol station attendant
Net wages: R10 400 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: 2 rooms in a backyard flat, water
slides.body: The landlady hasn't put it up in two years. I don't say anything in case that reminds her.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Pap, chicken feet, nappies, the kids' milk
slides.body: My wife does the list. I do the paying. Neither of us enjoys the till.

slides.title: Black tax
slides.includes: My father's medication, my brother's taxi money
slides.body: It goes by EFT on the 26th, before I can think about it.

slides.title: Taxi fare
slides.includes: Home to the garage and back, 26 days
slides.body: I start at 5 am. The first taxi is the only one that's full of people like me.

slides.title: Airtime & data
slides.includes: Me and my wife, WhatsApp bundles
slides.body: I buy it R10 at a time. I've never added it up. It's more than I thought.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Prepaid electricity, funeral policy, burial society, school stationery, haircuts
slides.body: The burial society is R150 and the funeral policy R280. I'd never go without either.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R10 400. Tips are in there too, about R400 on a good month, and that's the part I never plan around.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded my statement to Beyond Horizon and it sorted every transaction for me.

The airtime number was the one that surprised me.

No bank login needed.
